doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Selling bottles through the audience and pocketing extra money
summary: The musicians sold a dollar a bottle through the crowd, up to five or six hundred a night, and he hid his own stash in the weeds.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: a couple of steps he could do, you see, when he got through. See there? Now the boys will go through the audience, uh, this medicine that's one dollar a bottle. The boys will go through. All the musicians

would go? All of them would, we'd grab an armload of medicine, yeah. And go around. In fact, when this was going on, we had an armload of medicine there. And you just pass through the audience. All you
folks have a dollar. About how many would you sell on a good night? Oh, God. You do.

Five or six hundred dollars. That's money, huh? Oh, easy. On one night. Oh, yeah. Easy. Cleaning up, huh? Easy, because you're going through the audience, uh, three or four times during the show. Uh-huh. Then, uh, we would have a little, uh, stash out there in the weeds, you know. Usually we played empty lots. I'd have me some bottles out there hid. When I sold all the doc's medicine, I'd get mine. Made a little extra money. Did Doc know about that? No, he didn't know. I should say not. We'd set that deal early. And we'd make, uh, four or five dollars extra a night. You want the deal? So, and, uh, after the show, the band, uh, could play extra deals. Well. Extra jobs if he wanted to. In town. That's right. You mean he didn't object to that? Oh, no. I should say not. He'd be like, he'd play. What'd you do, go to a club or something? Yeah. What'd you put somebody for us? Yeah. Usually, when we hit a town, you know, the first night, we'd always look for the most prominent bootlegging joints. Uh-huh. And the leader of the band would look out for something like that, you know, and let it know.
